original_question: What donor nerve did Zuker et al. suggest in 1989 to restore the ability to smile in children with Möbius syndrome linked to maternal misoprostol use?

final_qi.question: What donor nerve did Zuker et al. suggest in 1989 to restore the ability to smile in children with Möbius syndrome linked to maternal misoprostol use?
final_qi.search_keyword: Zuker 1989 donor nerve restore smile Möbius syndrome maternal misoprostol
final_qi.long_answer: In his 1989 study, Zuker et al. suggested using the masseteric nerve as the donor nerve to restore smile function in children with Möbius syndrome linked to maternal misoprostol use. The masseteric nerve, a branch of the trigeminal nerve, offers a robust neural input capable of reinnervating a transplanted muscle, thereby achieving spontaneous and effective smile restoration in these patients.
